title: Autotuning mixed-precision KV profiles with prompt-drift-aware calibration and token-level accuracy telemetry
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build and evaluate an autotuning pipeline that selects per-request mixed-precision KV cache profiles (fp8, int8, or hybrid) based on prompt characteristics and live telemetry. We want to minimize end-to-end token latency and token-cost while bounding generation quality regressions (per-token and aggregated), and to make the selection robust to prompt drift over time.
updates: 2026-02-10 — Kickoff: scoped MLP consisting of two microbenchmarks + offline calibration harness. Agreed success criteria: <=2% aggregate quality drop on eval set, 10–30% median p99 token-latency reduction vs baseline fp16, and stable selection accuracy under drift.

2026-02-17 — Implementation: added mixed-precision runtime flags to kv-layer (per-KV-tensor dtype annotation + fallback to fp16). Instrumented token-level reference logits capture for accuracy deltas. Initial autotuner prototype uses a light decision tree based on prefix length, avg token entropy, and kv-size.

2026-02-24 — Calibration: created per-model calibration dataset sampler that stratifies by prompt length, domain (docs/chat/code), and input token entropy. Ran calibration sweep for 3 candidate quant maps: int8-uniform, fp8-e4m3, hybrid-per-layer (kv-only int8 for lower layers). Collected latency and top-k token divergence distributions.

2026-03-02 — Findings from sweep: int8-uniform reduces median latency by ~18% but shows a 3.5% token-level KL increase on informal-chat subset; fp8-e4m3 keeps KL <1% but tail latency improvement is only ~6%. Observed that long-prefix prompts amplify INT8 regressions due to KV magnitude variance.

2026-03-05 — Decision: implement prompt-drift detector (exponential window over live token divergences) and use conservative fallback to fp8 when drift is detected. Also opted to expose a per-service safety SLO config to cap allowable KL drift.

2026-03-10 — Integration: hooked autotuner into routing layer, started A/B test on 5% of traffic for two customer-simulated workloads. Added dashboards for per-route precision selection rate, p50/p95/p99 token latencies, and aggregated token-level accuracy deltas.
acceptance_criteria: Autotuner selects mixed-precision profile at request time with <5ms median decision overhead
Aggregated generation quality drop <=2% (measured by task-specific evals and token-level KL) when autotuner is enabled vs fp16 baseline
Median token-level p99 latency improvement >=10% for at least one representative workload without violating quality bound
Prompt-drift detector triggers fallback with >90% precision when induced drift simulations are run
Documentation and API flag added to runtime and included in release notes for runtime-1.20
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive int8 profiles provide cost and latency wins but require tighter calibration and monitoring. We will prioritize conservative hybrid profiles for high-SLA customers.
Next experiments: per-layer dynamic scaling calibration, augment autotuner with a lightweight learned selector (latency budget set) and run head-to-head against rule-based tree.
Follow-ups: add scheduled recalibration job to recompute quant params weekly per-route and a drift alert playbook for SREs.
